candidates.name: Stroke due to Patent Foramen Ovale (PFO)
support_spans: Transthoracic echocardiography with bubble study was unremarkable
A diagnosis of ischemic stroke in a 36‐year‐old gentleman with no apparent risk factors was made
candidates.why: The patient's young age and lack of traditional stroke risk factors suggest a possible cardiac source of embolism, such as a PFO.

candidates.name: Cavernous Malformation-Related Stroke
support_spans: Noncontrast CT of the head showed no acute pathology but revealed an incidental 4 × 6 mm hyperdense focus in the left parasagittal frontal cortex suggestive of a cavernoma
contradict_spans: Brain MRI showed a recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla without hemorrhagic transformation
candidates.why: The presence of a cavernoma in the patient's brain could be a potential source of stroke, although the location of the infarct does not directly correlate with the cavernoma.

candidates.name: Stroke of Other Determined Etiology
support_spans: A diagnosis of ischemic stroke in a 36‐year‐old gentleman with no apparent risk factors was made
further investigations were initiated to look for the cause
candidates.why: The patient's stroke may be due to a variety of other causes, such as vasculitis, dissection, or other rare conditions, which would require further investigation to determine.

key_evidence_spans: A 36‐year‐old man of Indian origin presented at 2:30 a.m. with acute right‐sided weakness and three episodes of vomiting
Noncontrast CT of the head showed no acute pathology but revealed an incidental 4 × 6 mm hyperdense focus in the left parasagittal frontal cortex suggestive of a cavernoma
Brain MRI showed a recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla without hemorrhagic transformation

candidates.name: Susac's syndrome
support_spans: bilateral torsional nystagmus on vertical and horizontal gaze
recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla
contradict_spans: no visual change or speech disturbance
candidates.why: The combination of stroke, nystagmus, and the patient's age suggests a rare condition like Susac's syndrome, which is characterized by microangiopathic changes in the brain, retina, and cochlea.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may deserve minority protection because it is a rare condition that can be easily missed, and the patient's presentation does not fit the typical pattern of atherosclerotic stroke.

candidates.name: Cavernous malformation-associated stroke
support_spans: incidental 4 × 6 mm hyperdense focus in the left parasagittal frontal cortex suggestive of a cavernoma
recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla
contradict_spans: CT angiography demonstrated normal opacification of cervical and intracranial arteries
candidates.why: The presence of a cavernoma and a recent ischemic stroke suggests that the cavernoma may be the source of the stroke, possibly due to hemorrhage or thrombosis.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may deserve minority protection because cavernous malformations are rare and can be asymptomatic, making it a less common cause of stroke that may be overlooked.

candidates.name: Fabry disease
support_spans: acute right‐sided weakness
odd sensations and occasional tremors in his right arm and leg over the prior two weeks
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms, including acute weakness and odd sensations, could be consistent with Fabry disease, a rare genetic disorder that can cause stroke and other neurological symptoms.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may deserve minority protection because Fabry disease is a rare condition that can be difficult to diagnose, and the patient's normal lipid profile does not rule out the diagnosis.
